title: Values, copies, and references (Go)
description: Go has garbage collection and no Rust-style ownership, but values vs pointers still shape how data is shared.
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## References vs primitives

Primitives copy by value; objects share references. `String` is immutable like Go strings.

exercises.title: String reassignment
exercises.description: Assign `s := "hi"`, assign `t := s`, print `t` with `System.out.print` (no newline).
hints: `t := s` copies the string header, both refer to same bytes

exercises.title: Slice header copy
exercises.description: Create `s := []int{1, 2}`, assign `t := s`, set `t[0] = 9`, print `s[0]` and `s[1]` concatenated as digits with `System.out.print` (no space, no newline) → `92`.

exercises.title: Int copy
exercises.description: `a := 3`, `b := a`, increment `b` with `b++`, print `a` and `b` space-separated with `System.out.print` (no trailing newline).
